items.title: Buckingham interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2019
items.q: They send it to Eddie Bayer... Then Michael Rhodes the bass player gets it and adds his part.

ctx.x: What would get you back into the studio now as a producer?

It would have to be an old friend wanting me to do something with them again. Because if it was a new artist now, honestly I wouldn’t know what to do — I mean I’d know what to do musically but I wouldn’t know what to do because the structure, the business has changed so dramatically since 2000, the year 2000. Particularly. I look at that as the watershed year because that’s when the kids came out with Napster and people were downloading music and the income just — they’re talking about now how streaming has…

sound of streamed music because of the compression that’s necessary. I don’t care for the way records are made in the most part. One of the students was asking me during the fire drill up here, how records are made. I said, “Well you know I know all the great players that are still around, but they rarely are called in to do live sessions anymore.
